title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: add FHS and LMP dissectors, reassemble and forward L2CAP
description:
Prevoiusly, the BR/EDR RF dissector just decoded the packet header and
displayed the rest of the packet as blob. It made no effort to further
decode the contents.

This commit adds a dissector for the Bluetooth BR/EDR FHS packets
used to exchange frequency hopping parameters during link
setup. Contents from the FHS packets are used to populate a table of
devices, containing the full device addresses, and a connection table
that links Master LAP and LT_ADDRs to connections. Normally, only the
lower 24 bits of the device address (LAP, lower address part) are used
in the packet preamble, but the upper part (UAP) is needed for example
as initialization value of the CRC.

This commit adds a payload header decoder, to determine how to route
the contents to downstream dissectors.

This commit further adds a dissector for the Bluetooth BR/EDR
LMP protocol, which is used to manage the BR/EDR link(s). Data from
LMP is used to find out about secondary LT_ADDRs for a device for eSCO
connections, keeping track of eSCO packet sizes.

This commit further adds reassembly of fragmented L2CAP packets, and
routes L2CAP traffic to the existing L2CAP dissector.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: No header for packets with inquiry access code
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: No header for packets with inquiry access code

Some "packets" have neither packet header nor payload. Unfortunately,
the BT BR/EDR pseudoheader has no flag whether there was a packet
header. Implement some heuristics to determine whether there was a
header. If the access code is one of the inquiry access code range,
there is usually no packet header unless it is an FHS packet.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: Header decode improvements
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: Header decode improvements

According to Vol 2 Part B Chapter 6.5.1.4, FHS packets should always
employ a HEC UAP equal to DCI (== 0x00). This patch therefore checks
the HEC checksum for FHS packets even if the UAP is not valid in the
pseudoheader.

The reverse_bits implementation has been made slightly more efficient.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: header decoding according to specification
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth BR/EDR RF: header decoding according to specification

According to the LINKTYPE_BLUETOOTH_BREDR_BB Packet Structure specification
(http://www.whiterocker.com/bt/LINKTYPE_BLUETOOTH_BREDR_BB.html), the
Bluetooth header should be formatted according to the Bluetooth
specification Volume 2, Part B, Section 6.4. However, right now
wireshark expects the header to be in a weird format,
specifically it expects the header fields to be MSB but the bits
within each header field to be LSB. (Bluetooth standard is all
LSB). Furthermore, it computes the HEC (header check, i.e. the header
CRC) with 4 bits arbitrarily masked.

This patch decodes the header according to the spec. It still accepts
the old format (if the broken HEC matches), and displays a warning.
